items.label: Major Field Electives
items.notes:
- CMPSC190AA-ZZ
Four units maximum from CMPSC 192 and 196 combined; only for students with GPA of 3.0 or higher.

nodes.title: Critical Artificial Intelligence
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.description: Artificial intelligence now affects nearly all aspects of human life and knowledge production, from labor to language, and from fundamental physics to the arts. The pivotal role of the humanities lies in the critical analysis of the specific cultural techniques emerging from this technical revolution: new methods of language processing, image production, scientific reasoning, and social control require new critical and historical approaches. This course provides an introduction to the history and theory of artificial intelligence from the perspective of the humanities. Participants will acquire the skills to analyze and understand the design and construction of machine learning systems, and their philosophical and political implications.

nodes.title: Artificial Intelligence Seminar
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.description: Introductory seminar designed to immerse students in the diverse interdisciplinary field of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Features guest lectures by faculty members from various departments affiliated with AI centers and research initiatives. Students gain exposure to foundational AI techniques and their wide-ranging applications, preparing them for potential engagement in AI research and related academic opportunities. Students complete reading assignments to deepen their understanding and participate actively in seminar discussions.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Science
nodes.description: Introduction to computer program development for students with little to no programming experience. Basic programming concepts, variables and expressions, data and control structures, algorithms, debugging, program design, and documentation.

nodes.title: Intermediate Python Programming
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: CMPSC 8 or CMPSC W8 or ENGR 3 or ENGR W3 or ECE 3 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Intermediate topics in Computer Science using the Python programming language. Topics include object oriented programming, runtime analysis, data structures, and software testing methodologies.

nodes.title: Problem Solving with Computers I
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 3A or 2A with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently), CS 8 or Engineering 3 or ECE 3 with a grade of C or better, or significant prior programming experience.
nodes.description: Fundamental building blocks for solving problems using computers. Topics include basic computer organization and programming constructs: memory CPU, binary arithmetic, variables, expressions, statements, conditionals, iteration, functions, parameters, recursion, primitive and composite data types, and basic operating system and debugging tools.

nodes.title: Problem Solving with Computers II
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better; and Mathematics 3B or 2B with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Intermediate building blocks for solving problems using computers. Topics include intermediate object-oriented programming, data structures, object-oriented design, algorithms for manipulating these data structures and their run-time analyses. Data structures introduced include stacks, queues, lists, trees, and sets.

nodes.title: Data Programming and Analytics for Artificial Intelligence
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: CMPSC 9 or CMPSC 24 with a grade of C or better; and, Mathematics 3A or 2A with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Course delves into essential programming, algorithmic, and data analytics techniques foundational to artificial intelligence. Topics include data acquisition, cleaning, transformation, modeling, sampling, visualization and simulation, statistical programming, hypothesis testing, inference, with applications in artificial intelligence. Students will apply these concepts through hands-on Python projects, gaining practical experience in using data analytics to develop intelligent systems.

nodes.title: Object Oriented Design and Implementation
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 24 with a grade of C or better
nodes.description: Advanced topics in object-oriented computing. Topics include encapsulation, data hiding, inheritance, polymorphism, compilation, linking and loading, memory management, and debugging; recent advances in design and development tools, practices, libraries, and operating system support.

nodes.title: Foundations of Computer Science
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better and Mathematics 4A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the theoretical underpinnings of computer science. Topics include propositional predicate logic, set theory, functions and relations, counting, mathematical induction and recursion (generating functions).

nodes.title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better and Mathematics 4A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introductory discrete mathematics. Topics include fundamental principles of counting (permutations, combinations), sets, graph theory, elementary probability, and number theory.

nodes.title: Logic and Automata
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 41; open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only.

items.text: open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only

nodes.description: Introduction to formal logic and computational theory. Covers propositional and predicate logic and select topics from formal languages and automata theory, including regular, context-free languages, and Turing Machines.

nodes.title: Computer Organization and Logic Design
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better; and Mathematics 3C or 4A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Assembly language programming and advanced computer organization; digital logic design topics including gates, combinational circuits, flip-flops, and the design and analysis of sequential circuits.

nodes.title: Introduction to Research in Computer Science
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 40 and Computer Science 32; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Defining a CS research problem, finding and reading technical papers, oral communication, technical writing, and independent learning. Course participants work in teams as they apprentice with a CS research group to propose an original research problem and write a research proposal.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computational Science
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B with a grade of C or better; Mathematics 6A with a grade of C or better; Computer Science 24 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the numerical algorithms that form the foundations of data science, machine learning, and computational science and engineering. Matrix computation, linear equation systems, eigenvalue and singular value decompositions, numerical optimization. The informed use of mathematical software environments and libraries, such as python/numpy/scipy.

nodes.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: CMPSC 40 or CMPSC 41 or MATH 8 with a grade of C or better; CMPSC 24 or CMPSC 25 with a grade of C or better; PSTAT 120A or ECE 139 (may be taken concurrently with CMPSC 130A); open to Computer Science Department majors, and Electrical and Computer Engineering Department majors only.

items.text: open to Computer Science Department majors, and Electrical and Computer Engineering Department majors only

nodes.description: Data structures and applications with proofs of correctness and analysis. Hash Tables, Priority Queues (heaps); Balanced Search Trees. Graph Traversal techniques and their applications.

nodes.title: Algorithm Design and Analysis
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A.
nodes.description: Design and analysis of computer algorithms. Correctness proofs and solution of recurrence relations. Design techniques; divide and conquer, greedy strategies, dynamic programming. Applications of techniques to problems from several disciplines. NP - completeness.

nodes.title: Algorithms Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.description: Applying theoretical knowledge about algorithms, data structures, and complexity to performing the complete process of analyzing a computational problem, estimating the running time of suggested solutions, and implementing an effective and correct program for the computational problem.

nodes.title: Randomized Algorithms
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: CMPSC 130B with a letter grade of B or better.
nodes.description: Covers advanced algorithmic ideas, focusing on randomized algorithms. Explores how randomization can be used to make algorithms simpler and more efficient, and to understand the probabilistic analysis of algorithms.

nodes.title: Mathematics of Artificial Intelligence
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Math 4A; CMPSC 25 or CMPSC 24; and ECE 139.
nodes.description: Comprehensive mathematical foundation for machine learning and AI. Covers key topics in statistics, linear algebra, and optimization as applied to modern AI systems. Topics include quantifying bias and variance, estimation theory (e.g., maximum likelihood estimation, ensemble methods), statistics on graphs, including the configuration model, probability distributions on graphs, summary statistics, and random walks. Optimization topics include gradient descent, continuous and convex optimization, backpropagation, kernel methods, and practical aspects of optimization.

nodes.title: Automata and Formal Languages
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 40 or Computer Science 41 with a grade of C or better; open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only.

items.text: open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only

nodes.description: Formal languages; finite automata and regular expressions; properties of regular languages; pushdown automata and context-free grammars; properties of context-free languages; introduction to Turing machines and computability.

nodes.title: Parallel Computing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: MATH 4A with a grade C or better; and, CMPSC 32 or CMPSC 130A.
nodes.description: Fundamentals of parallel programming and algorithm design to speedup machine learning and scientific computation. Topics include parallel architectures with shared memory machines and clusters, GPUs, message-passing and thread programming, parallel performance evaluation and optimization, parallelization of core matrix algorithms in machine learning and scientific computing applications, and MapReduce programming for data-intensive cloud computing.

nodes.title: Computer Science Project
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 32 with a grade of C or better; open to Computer Science majors only.

items.text: open to Computer Science majors only

nodes.description: Team-based project development. Topics include software engineering and professional development practices, interface design, advanced library support; techniques for team oriented design and development, testing and test driven development, and software reliability and robustness. Students present and demonstrate final projects.

nodes.title: Hardware/Software Interface
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper division standing in Computer Science, ComputerEngineering, or Electrical Engineering. Familiarity with C, FiniteAutomata, and Computer Architecture.
nodes.description: Design and coding of embedded programs. Real-time constraints and management of resources. Practical I/O interfaces and protocols, polling, interrupt maintenance, atomic code, blocking and non-blocking tasks. Static and dynamic task scheduling under real-time and limited resource constraints.

nodes.title: Computer Architecture
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 32 with a grade of C or better; Computer Science 64 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the architecture of computer systems. Topics include: central processing units, memory systems, channels and controllers, peripheral devices, interrupt systems, software versus hardware tradeoffs.

nodes.title: Advanced Applications Programming
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 24 and 32 with a grade of C or better; open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only.

items.text: open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only

nodes.description: Advanced application programming using a high-level, virtual-machine-based language. Topics include generic programming, exception handling, automatic memory management, and application development, management, and maintenance tools, third-party library use, version control, software testing, issue tracking, code review, and working with legacy code.

nodes.title: Translation of Programming Languages
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 64 or Electrical Engineering 154 or Electrical Engineering 154A; Computer Science 130A; and Computer Science 138; open to computer science and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to computer science and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Study of the structure of compilers. Topics include: lexical analysis; syntax analysis including LL and LR parsers; type checking; run-time environments; intermediate code generation; and compiler-construction tools.

nodes.title: Programming Languages
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A and 138; open to computer science and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to computer science and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Concepts of programming languages: scopes, parameter passing, storage management; control flow, exception handling; encapsulation and modularization mechanisms; reusability through genericity and inheritance; type systems; programming paradigms (imperative, object-oriented, functional, and others). Emerging programming languages and their development infrastructures.

nodes.title: Artificial Intelligence
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A and PSTAT 120A
nodes.description: Introduction to the field of artificial intelligence, which seeks to understand and build intelligent computational systems. Topics include intelligent agents, problem solving and heuristic search, knowledge representation and reasoning, uncertainty and probabilistic reasoning, machine learning, reinforcement learning, and responsible AI.

nodes.title: Machine Learning
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A.
nodes.description: Covers the most important techniques of machine learning (ML) and includes discussions of: well-posed learning problems; artificial neural networks; concept learning and general to specific ordering; decision tree learning; genetic algorithms; Bayesian learning; analytical learning; and others.

nodes.title: Operating Systems
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A; and, Computer Science 154 or ECE 154A (may be taken concurrently); open to computer science, computer engineering or electrical engineering majors only.

items.text: open to computer science, computer engineering or electrical engineering majors only

nodes.description: Basic concepts of operating systems. The notion of a process; interprocess communication and synchronization; input-output, file systems, memory management.

nodes.title: Distributed Systems
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A.
nodes.description: Distributed systems architecture, distributed programming, network of computers, message passing, remote procedure calls, group communication, naming and membership problems, asynchrony, logical time, consistency, fault-tolerance, and recovery.

nodes.title: Software Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A. Open to Computer Science or Computer Engineering majors only, or by consent of department.

items.text: Open to Computer Science or Computer Engineering majors only, or by consent of department

nodes.description: Software engineering is concerned with long-term, large-scale programming projects. Software management, cost estimates, problem specification and analysis, system design techniques, system testing and performance evaluation, and system maintenance. Students will design, manage, and implement a medium-sized project.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Database Systems
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A.
nodes.description: Database system architectures, relational data model, relational algebra, relational calculus, SQL, QBE, query processing, integrity constraints (key constraints, referential integrity), database design, ER and object- oriented data model, functional dependence, lossless join and dependency preserving decompositions, Boyce-Codd and Third Normal Forms.

nodes.title: Design and Implementation Techniques of Database Systems
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 130B.
nodes.description: Queries and processing, optimizer, cost models, execution plans, rewriting rules, access methods, spatial indexing; transactions, ACID properties, concurrency control, serializability, two-phase locking, timestamping, logging,checkpointing, transaction abort and commit, crash recovery; distributed databases.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Communication Networks
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: CMPSC 32 with a grade of C or better; PSTAT 120A or ECE 139; open to computer science, electrical engineering, and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to computer science, electrical engineering, and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Basic concepts in networking, the OSI model, error detection codes, flow control, routing, medium access control, and high-speed networks.

nodes.title: Network Computing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 176A.
nodes.description: Focus on networking and web technologies used in the Internet. The class covers socket programming and web-based techniques that are used to build distributed applications.

nodes.title: Advanced Topics in Internet Computing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 176A.
nodes.description: General overview of wireless and mobile networking, multimedia, security, multicast, quality of service, IPv6, and web caching. During the second half of the course, one or more of the above are studied in greater detail.

nodes.title: Computer Security
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 170 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Introduction to the basics of computer security and privacy. Analysis of technical difficulties of producing secure computer information systems that provide guaranteed controlled sharing. Examination and critique of current systems, methods, certification.

nodes.title: Introduction to Cryptography
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 24 with a grade of C or better; Computer Science 40 or Computer Science 41 with a grade of C or better; and PSTAT 120A or 121A or ECE 139 or permission of instructor.
nodes.description: An introduction to the basic concepts and techniques of cryptography and cryptanalysis. Topics include: The Shannon Theory, classical systems, the enigma machine, the data encryption standard, public key systems, digital signatures, file security.

nodes.title: Computer Graphics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Overview of OpenGL graphics standard, OpenGL statemachine, other 3D graphics libraries, 3D graphicspipeline, 3D transformations and clipping, colormodel, shading model, shadow algorithms, texturing,curves and curved surfaces, graphics hardware,interaction devices and techniques

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Vision
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing in Artificial Intelligence, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.
nodes.description: Overview of computer vision problems and techniques for analyzing the content of images and video. Topics include image formation, edge detection, image segmentation, pattern recognition, texture analysis, optical flow, stereo vision, shape representation and recovery techniques, issues in object recognition, and case studies of practical vision systems.

nodes.title: Ethics, Privacy, Fairness, and Bias in AI and Computing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: CMPSC 25.
nodes.description: Multifaceted ethical considerations of artificial intelligence, focusing on privacy, bias, fairness, and transparency. Students engage in hands-on learning by examining practical tools and frameworks like AWS, Azure, and GCP, gaining insights into best practices for mitigating data privacy risks, detecting and managing bias, ensuring fairness, and monitoring model performance. Through case studies, discussions, and exercises, course addresses real-world challenges such as data poisoning, feature drift, and human oversight in decision-making processes. Explores key algorithms and methodologies for model explainability, including fairness and bias detection techniques, to develop a holistic understanding of responsible AI.

nodes.title: Mobile Application Development
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 56 or Computer Science 156; and Computer Science 130A.
nodes.description: Introduction to programming mobile computing devices. Learn about and study the shift in software development from desktop to mobile device applications. Topics include software engineering and design practices, advances in programming practice, and support tools for mobile application development and testing. Students develop and deploy mobile applications as part of their course work.

nodes.title: Human-Computer Interaction
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper division standing; Open to computer science, computer engineering, and electrical engineering majors.

items.text: Open to computer science, computer engineering, and electrical engineering majors

nodes.description: The study of human-computer interaction enables system architects to design useful, efficient, and enjoyable computer interfaces. This course teaches the theory, design guidelines, programming practices, and evaluation procedures behind effective human interaction with computers.

nodes.title: Internet of Things (IoT) Systems
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: CMPSC 32 or CMPSC 130A.
nodes.description: The Internet of Things (IoT) embeds ordinary physical objects in our environment with digital intelligence -- via sensing, control, communications, and computing capabilities. As such, IoT advances are likely key drivers of the next computing revolution. This course will teach IoT systems end-to-end, including the fundamentals of IoT devices, software architectures, communication protocols, security approaches, distributed, multi-tier (e.g. sensors, edge, and cloud) programming and deployment considerations needed to support emerging IoT applications.

nodes.title: Deep Learning
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: CMPSC 165B.
nodes.description: Deep Learning has been driving the progress of AI in the past decade and has found versatile applications in many products and everyday life. This course will introduce general principles, methods, network architectures, and applications of Deep Learning. Covers neural network architectures including convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, Transformer, and graph neural networks. Covers techniques for designing loss, training, and inference methods. Focus on both the principles, analytical skills, and implementation practice. Suitable for undergraduate and graduate students who want to pursue a career in AI or conduct research in deep learning.

nodes.title: Introduction to Natural Language Processing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Prerequisites: CMPSC 130A, CMPSC 165A, and CMPSC 165B.
nodes.description: This NLP course explores AI's capability to understand human language, focusing on machine learning algorithms and large language models. It covers language modeling, sentiment analysis, tagging, and machine translation, discussing lexical, syntactic, and semantic processing. Key models include Naive Bayes, logistic regression, and neural networks like RNNs and CNNs. It emphasizes empirical analysis of text corpora and how to evaluate the strengths and limitations of statistical tools, including large language models, in NLP.

nodes.title: Projects in Computer Science
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Projects in computer science for advanced undergraduate students.

nodes.title: Undergraduate Research
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Students must: (1) have attained upper-division standing (2) have a minimum3.0 grade-point average for preceding three quarters, (3) have consent of instructor.

items.text: Students must: (1) have attained upper-division standing (2) have a minimum3.0 grade-point average for preceding three quarters

nodes.description: Research opportunities for undergraduate students. Students will be expected to giveregular oral presentations, actively participate in a weekly seminar, and prepare at least one written report on their research.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Science
nodes.description: Introduction to computer program development for students with little to no programming experience. Basic programming concepts, variables and expressions, data and control structures, algorithms, debugging, program design, and documentation.

nodes.title: Introduction to Python Programming For Engineers
nodes.prereq_text: Open to EE and CMPEN majors only.

requires.text: Open to EE and CMPEN majors only

nodes.description: This course represents a comprehensive foundation for core ECE topics in signal processing, image analysis, machine learning, optimization and control. The lectures present concepts from linear algebra, such as matrix computations, systems of linear equations, eigenspace decomposition, inner-product, orthogonality, least-squares and linear regression. Students actively engage with the technical materials with an introduction to Python programming and associated hands-on sessions. The materials are be motivated by real-world scenarios ranging from medical imaging to autonomous vehicles, from (miscarriage of) justice to brain-machine interfaces, from music analysis to GPS design.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits & Systems
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or Mathematics 3AH-BH, and Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 3C, all with a minimum grade of C; and, Math 4B or 4BI or 5A with a minimum grade of C (may be taken concurrently); Physics 3, 7B or 23 (may be taken concurrently); open only to electrical engineering and computer engineering majors.

items.text: open only to electrical engineering and computer engineering majors

nodes.description: The objective of the course is to establish the foundations of analog and digital circuits. The course will introduce the student to the power of abstraction, resistive networks, network analysis, nonlinear analysis and the digital abstraction.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems Lab
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10A (may be taken concurrently) with a C- or better grade.
nodes.description: The goal of 10AL is to provide the student with a hands-on application of the concepts discussed in ECE 10A. The lab will introduce the use of microcontrollers as a data acquisition system, network analysis, resistors, nonlinear analysis and digital abstraction.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Logic Design
nodes.prereq_text: Open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and pre-computer engineering majors only.

requires.text: Open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and pre-computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Boolean algebra, logic of propositions, minterm and maxterm expansions, Karnaugh maps, Quine-McCluskey method, melti-level circuits, combinational circuit design and simulation, multiplexers, decoders, programmable logic devices.

nodes.title: Probability and Statistics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR
nodes.prereq_text: Open to Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering and pre-Computer Engineering majors only.

requires.text: Open to Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering and pre-Computer Engineering majors only

nodes.description: Fundamentals of probability, conditional probability, Bayes rule, random variables, functions of random variables, expectation and high-order moments, Markov chains, hypothesis testing.

nodes.title: Digital Design Principles
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 15A and ECE 2A or ECE 10A & ECE 10AL with a minimum grade of C- in each course; or Computer Science 30 or 64 with a minimum grade of C- in each course; open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and computer science majors only.

items.text: open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and computer science majors only

nodes.description: Design of synchronous digital systems: timing diagrams, propagation delay, latches and flip-flops, shift registers and counters, Mealy/Moore finite state machines, Verilog, 2-phase clocking, timing analysis, CMOS implementation, S-RAM, RAM-based designs, ASM charts, state minimization.

nodes.title: Hardware/Software Interface
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper division standing in Computer Engineering, Computer Science and Electrical Engineering. Familiarity with C, FiniteAutomata, and Computer Architecture.
nodes.description: Design and coding of embedded programs. Real-time constraints and management of resources. Practical I/O interfaces and protocols, polling, interrupt maintenance, atomic code, blocking and non-blocking tasks. Static and dynamic task scheduling under real-time and limited resource constraints.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Architecture
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 152A with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE and CMPEN majors only.

items.text: open to EE and CMPEN majors only

nodes.description: Instruction-set architecture (ISA) and computer performance; Machine instructions, assembly, addressing modes; Memory map,arrays, pointers; Procedure calls; Number formats; Simple ALUs; Data path,control, microprogram; Buses, I/O programming, interrupts; Pipelined data paths and control schemes.

nodes.title: INTRODUCTION TO DEEP LEARNING
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Open to EE, Computer Engineering and Computer Science with upper-division standing.

items.text: Open to EE, Computer Engineering and Computer Science with

nodes.description: Introduction to multilayered neural networks, early models of perceptrons and associative memory; back-propagation learning; convolutional neural networks; recurrent neural networks; attention models; applications to natural language processing and computer vision.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Vision
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing in Artificial Intelligence, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.
nodes.description: Overview of computer vision problems and techniques for analyzing the content of images and video. Topics include image formation, edge detection, image segmentation, pattern recognition, texture analysis, optical flow, stereo vision, shape representation and recovery techniques, issues in object recognition, and case studies of practical vision systems.

nodes.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 139 or PSTAT 120A or equivalent.
nodes.description: An introductory course to topics in machine learning studied from a probability theory viewpoint. Covers an overview of basic probability, inference and estimation, regression algorithms, Markov chains, inference for Markov models and the EM algorithm, Markov decision process, and reinforcement learning. In addition to covering mathematical and algorithmic details, the course includes several hands-on projects to implement the machine learning algorithms.

nodes.title: Introduction to Literary Study
nodes.prereq_text: Writing 2.
nodes.description: Acquaints students with purposes and tools of literary interpretation. Introduces techniques and vocabulary of analytic discussion and critical writing. Some emphasis on poetry with attention also to drama, essay, and the novel.

nodes.title: Literature and/of Artificial Intelligence
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Writing 2 or upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Agency, one of the key literary and philosophical problems, has a new dimension in the era of so-termed artificial intelligence. So, too, the old questionwhat is the value and purpose of human life resonates differently when considered in light of mass automation. The imagination, and the realization, of artificial entities, are not new, but the exponential developments in the machine and deep learning over the past decade, along with an evolving understanding of cognition, do invite us to reevaluate the mythologies we have built up around them. What texts and concepts inform our understanding of intentional action and life itself in the present?

nodes.title: Data Stories: Theory and Practice of Data-driven Narratives in the Digital Age
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Writing 2 or upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Data Stories introduces students to an increasingly important genre of discourse in todays society: data-driven narrative--e.g., as it appears in journalism; science, medical, and political reporting; business or government writing; and even some literary and artistic forms. The course brings humanities approaches such as narrative theory, genre theory, and media theory into conjunction with readings about data journalism and data visualization to ask this central question: how do you make a good story out of data? Among other assignments, students create a project in which they take a dataset and make a narrative about it.

nodes.title: Upper-Division Seminar
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Writing 2 or 50 or 109 or English 10 or upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Content will vary with each instructor. Students will be asked to do a project that acquaints them with some of the resources of the library and results in their reading beyond the primary course materials. A full description for any given quarter will be available on the English Departments website.

nodes.title: Introduction to Programming
nodes.description: General philosophy of programming and problem-solving. Students will be introduced to the programming language MATLAB. Specific areas of study will include algorithms, basic decision structures, arrays, matrices, and graphing.

nodes.title: Introduction to Programming
nodes.description: General philosophy of programming and problem-solving. Students will be introduced to the programming language MATLAB. Specific areas of study will include algorithms, basic decision structures, arrays, matrices, and graphing.

nodes.title: Critical Artificial Intelligence
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.description: Artificial intelligence now affects nearly all aspects of human life and knowledge production, from labor to language, and from fundamental physics to the arts. The pivotal role of the humanities lies in the critical analysis of the specific cultural techniques emerging from this technical revolution: new methods of language processing, image production, scientific reasoning, and social control require new critical and historical approaches. This course provides an introduction to the history and theory of artificial intelligence from the perspective of the humanities. Participants will acquire the skills to analyze and understand the design and construction of machine learning systems, and their philosophical and political implications.

nodes.title: Machine Learning
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Major Field Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 17; or consent of instructor
nodes.description: Introduces students to machine learning and deep learning. ME 107 is taught at the undergraduate level and teaches students how to identify a machine learning problem in the context of real-world applications, mathematically formulate a learning problem, identify when a learning problem is well-posed, under-determined and overdetermined, and develop algorithms and Python code to solve the problem. Students are introduced to the concepts of learning algorithms, overfitting, under-fitting, statistical measures of estimators, optimization approaches to learning, principal component analysis, regression, support vector machines, and artificial neural networks.
